card.name: Thang Ta
card.tagline: Manipuri sword-and-spear martial art and dance
card.profile: Thang-Ta (Meitei: thang = sword, ta = spear) is the armed component of the classical Meitei martial art Huyen Langlon of Manipur (the unarmed component is Sarit Sarak) (Wikipedia: Huyen langlon; Impart). It encompasses spear and sword combat, war dances (the sword dance Thangkairol and spear dance Khousarol), and esoteric ritual practice. It peaked under King Khagemba (r. 1597-1652) and the duelling ethics were codified in the 16th-17th-century Chainarol; banned by the British after the 1891 Anglo-Manipuri War, it was reintroduced by Maharaja Churachand in 1934. Weapons include a bamboo double-bladed spear, round shield (chungoi) and swords; it underlies classical Manipuri dance and influenced Pung Cholom (Impart).
card.insight: Thang-Ta blends combat technique with ritual and dance - its decorative sword sequences (Leiteng-thang) are performance-oriented while the Yanna-thang are true combat forms, reflecting its dual martial and artistic identity (Impart).
